title: Meeting Handover & Offboarding: Preserve Deal Context When Reps Leave
summary: When a rep leaves, their deal context walks out with them. Here's how to preserve every conversation, scorecard, and CRM note so handovers don't tank pipeline.
body_markdown:
When a sales rep leaves, their open pipeline doesn't just change hands. Most of the deal context walks out the door with them. The CRM notes are thin, the champion relationships are undocumented, and the next rep inherits a list of names with dollar signs attached.


The fix isn't a better offboarding checklist. Capture every customer conversation before anyone gives notice — recorded, scored, and searchable.


**Short answer:** A proper sales handover preserves three things: the full conversation record (every call, transcript, and summary), the deal-level context (champion, pain, next steps, risks), and the CRM state (fields updated, activities logged). If any of those three live only in the departing rep's head or inbox, the handover will fail. Capture them continuously, not at the exit interview.


## Why most sales handovers fail


Sales turnover is the highest of any white-collar function. Annual rep turnover averages[35%](https://stealthagents.com/research/cost-of-hiring-a-sales-representative-2026) , and[45% of B2B sales organizations](https://getgangly.com/blog/sales-rep-turnover-statistics) report turnover above 30%. For field sales,[41% of teams lose half their reps or more](https://www.convex.com/blog/cost-of-sales-rep-turnover-commercial-services) in a single year. A 10-person team hands over three to four territories annually — and probably more deals than that.


The fully loaded replacement cost per departure runs[$115,000–$150,000](https://getgangly.com/blog/sales-rep-turnover-statistics) . That number counts recruiting, ramp, and lost quota. It doesn't count the deals that die during the handover because the new rep had no idea what was discussed on the last three calls.


Most handovers fail for the same three reasons:


1. **The CRM is lying.** Reps update Salesforce or HubSpot when they have time, which is rarely. By the time someone leaves, the opportunity record reflects what the rep remembered to type, not what happened on the call.
2. **The conversation history is trapped.** Call recordings sit in individual notetaker accounts (Fathom, Granola, Otter) tied to the departing rep's email. When IT revokes access on day one, the record goes with it.
3. **The relationship map is in the rep's head.** Who's the champion? Who's the blocker? What did the economic buyer say in the last pricing conversation? None of that is written down.


The inheriting rep spends weeks re-discovering what the account already told the company. Deals slip. Some die. The customer feels like they're starting over — because they are.


## What a complete handover record looks like


A proper handover isn't a document the departing rep writes in their last week. It's a system that captures everything continuously, so the handover is already done by the time anyone resigns.


Three layers:


**Layer 1: The conversation record.** Every call recorded, transcribed, and summarized — video calls, phone calls, in-person meetings, field visits. Not in a personal notetaker account. In a company-owned, permissioned record. The new rep should be able to search “pricing objection” across the account's history and find the exact 90 seconds where the CFO pushed back.


**Layer 2: The deal state.** Scorecard against your methodology (MEDDIC, BANT, Challenger, or your own). Not a one-time snapshot — a running score across every call, so the inheriting rep can see how the deal progressed, where it's stuck, and which qualification criteria are still soft.


**Layer 3: The CRM truth.** Fields updated after every call, not at quarter-end. Next steps, risks, champion status, decision timeline — all current, all synced, all auditable.


With those three layers intact, the handover meeting takes 20 minutes: here's the account, here's every conversation, here's where it stands. Without them, the handover takes weeks and the deal probably dies.

## The 30-day handover playbook


The right tooling handles the record. The human handover still needs structure. Here's the sequence:


**Week before departure (if planned):**


- Departing rep records a 10-minute Loom per top-10 account: current status, champion name, next planned action, biggest risk. Nothing more. Everything else lives in the conversation record.
- Manager runs AI Deal Insights across the departing rep's pipeline to surface deals already at risk.
- RevOps confirms CRM is current (AI CRM Concierge makes this a non-event).


**Day of handover:**


- New rep gets access to the account's full conversation history, scorecards, and CRM record.
- 30-minute live handover meeting per top-10 account — not to transfer knowledge, but to align on next-step ownership.
- Email sent to every active champion from both reps on the same thread. Not “I'm leaving, here's your new rep” — “we're a team, here's who's running point now.”


**First 30 days post-handover:**


- New rep listens to the last three calls per inherited deal before any outbound action. 20 minutes per account.
- AI Coach scores the new rep's first calls on inherited deals; manager reviews to confirm the new rep is continuing from where the old rep left off, not restarting discovery.
- AI Deal Insights alerts route to the new rep's manager for the first 30 days, so inherited risks don't slip through during ramp.


For unplanned departures — fired, no notice — the playbook compresses to the same 30 days post-handover. It only works if the conversation record and CRM are already current. If they're not, you're not doing a handover; you're doing archaeology.


## Handovers also matter beyond offboarding


The same system that protects you during turnover works for every other handover:


- **AE to CS at closed-won.** The onboarding team inherits the full discovery and pricing history, not a one-page summary.
- **SDR to AE at qualification.** The AE listens to the SDR's discovery call before the first demo. No re-qualification needed.
- **Rep to manager escalation.** The manager pulls up the deal's conversation history and sees exactly where it stuck, in minutes.
- **Vacation and parental leave coverage.** Someone carries the account for a quarter without the customer feeling abandoned.


Teams that build this system get the offboarding use case for free. Teams that only think about it when someone resigns are already late.
